lines.trans: Whisper, both of you—it is only half past six on Saturday morning!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: Help me lift table number one aside gently so the legs do not scrape.
Read the postcard clue one more time before I touch the stones, Clara.
The retired mapmaker wrote: Count three flat stones north from the old shade tree.
Which way is north in my own courtyard? Where did my glasses go?
Your glasses are sitting above your eyebrows, Ernesto, and north faces the front gate.
Stone one, stone two, and here is stone three with the loose mortar edge.
Tap the middle with your wooden handle, Mateo—does it really sound hollow?
Listen to that clear echo underneath: there is a small space below this stone.
Nobody has lifted this flagstone since that rainy May thirty summers ago!

words.gloss: ago (hace treinta años = thirty years ago)

lines.trans: Please be careful, Mateo, because replacement courtyard stones cost a small fortune!
Stand back half a step while I slide the flat bar under the corner.

words.gloss: give; take (dad medio paso = take half a step)
corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

lines.trans: See you soon!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.text: Llegué diez minutos antes.
examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner for distant space or past time (aquella, aquellos, aquellas).

examples.text: Recuerdo muy bien aquel domingo.
examples.trans: I remember that Sunday very well.

examples.text: Aquella casa tiene cien años.
examples.trans: That house over there is a hundred years old.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Indicates position or movement toward the rear.

examples.text: Da un paso atrás, por favor.
examples.trans: Take one step back, please.

examples.text: Hombros atrás y respira hondo.
examples.trans: Shoulders back and breathe deeply.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; ayudar a + infinitive.

examples.text: ¿Te ayudo con esas dos cajas?
examples.trans: Shall I help you with those two boxes?

examples.text: Siempre ayudamos a los nuevos vecinos.
examples.trans: We always help the new neighbours.

meanings.note: Bajo llave means 'under lock and key'; as an adjective (bajo/baja), means 'low' or 'ground' (planta baja).

examples.text: Nos sentamos bajo el limonero.
examples.trans: We sit under the lemon tree.

examples.text: Guarda la caja bajo llave.
examples.trans: Keep the box under lock and key.

barra.gloss: bar; pry bar; loaf (of bread); counter

meanings.en: bar; pry bar; loaf (of bread); counter
meanings.note: Versatile feminine noun: una barra de hierro ('an iron bar'), una barra de pan ('a baguette/loaf'), or la barra del café ('the café counter').

examples.text: Mateo metió la barra plana de hierro bajo la piedra.
examples.trans: Mateo slid the flat iron bar under the stone.

examples.text: Compramos dos barras de pan recién horneado.
examples.trans: We bought two loaves of freshly baked bread.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (el borde de la mesa / de la ventana).

examples.text: No dejes el vaso lleno tan cerca del borde.
examples.trans: Do not leave the full glass so close to the edge.

examples.text: Lijamos suaves los bordes de madera antes de pintar.
examples.trans: We sanded the wooden edges smooth before painting.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.text: La calle está aquí.
examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine form: la cartógrafa.

examples.text: El cartógrafo dibujó cada calle estrecha del casco antiguo.
examples.trans: The mapmaker drew every narrow street of the old quarter.

examples.text: Aquel viajero era un joven cartógrafo que hacía mapas a mano.
examples.trans: That traveller was a young mapmaker who drew maps by hand.

meanings.note: Usually used in the plural (las cejas); arquear las cejas means 'to raise one's eyebrows'.

examples.text: Ernesto lleva las gafas puestas encima de las cejas.
examples.trans: Ernesto has his glasses sitting above his eyebrows.

examples.text: Levantó una ceja con gesto de sorpresa.
examples.trans: She raised an eyebrow with a surprised look.

meanings.note: El centro is downtown.

examples.text: El centro está aquí.
examples.trans: The city centre is here.

examples.text: Vemos los centros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the city centres from the door.

meanings.note: Alto y claro = loud and clear; ¡Claro! / ¡Pues claro! = Of course!

examples.text: El mensaje es alto y claro.
examples.trans: The message is loud and clear.

examples.text: ¡Pues claro que puedes pasar!
examples.trans: Well of course you can come in!

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: cuento).

examples.text: Mi abuela cuenta historias preciosas.
examples.trans: My grandmother tells lovely stories.

examples.text: Conté doce tazas en el armario.
examples.trans: I counted twelve cups in the cupboard.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: cuesta).

examples.text: El desayuno cuesta seis euros.
examples.trans: Breakfast costs six euros.

examples.text: Todo el pedido costó treinta euros.
examples.trans: The whole order cost thirty euros.

meanings.note: Con cuidado = carefully; ¡Cuidado con...! = Mind the...!

examples.text: El cuidado es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The care is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el cuidado.
examples.trans: We talk about the care.

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Debajo de + noun means 'underneath something'.

examples.text: Hay una llave pegada debajo.
examples.trans: There is a key taped underneath.

examples.text: Mira debajo de las ruedas.
examples.trans: Look underneath the wheels.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Marks a starting point in space or time.

examples.text: No hablamos desde aquel domingo.
examples.trans: We have not spoken since that Sunday.

examples.text: Abrimos al público desde mañana.
examples.trans: We open to the public starting tomorrow.

meanings.note: Everyday single-word opposite of rápido.

examples.text: Camina despacio por las escaleras.
examples.trans: Walk slowly on the stairs.

examples.text: Gira la rueda muy despacio.
examples.trans: Turn the wheel very slowly.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.text: Mira dónde señala con el lápiz.
examples.trans: Look where he is pointing with his pencil.

examples.text: ¿Dónde van las cucharillas y las servilletas?
examples.trans: Where do the teaspoons and the napkins go?

meanings.note: Reflected sound in a courtyard or hall.

examples.text: El eco está aquí.
examples.trans: The echo is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ecos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the echos from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Por encima = on top / over the surface.

examples.text: Pon azúcar glas por encima.
examples.trans: Put powdered sugar on top.

examples.text: Hay un cartel encima de la puerta.
examples.trans: There is a sign above the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle escrito.

examples.text: Escribo la nota con lápiz azul.
examples.trans: I write the note in blue pencil.

examples.text: Mi hermano me escribió una postal corta.
examples.trans: My brother wrote me a short postcard.

meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'to' before things (escucha el agua).

examples.text: Escucho los pájaros desde mi cama.
examples.trans: I listen to the birds from my bed.

examples.text: Escuchamos la lluvia sobre las tejas.
examples.trans: We listened to the rain on the tiles.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.text: Pásame ese cuaderno azul.
examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

esquina.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

meanings.en: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)
meanings.note: Outer corner where two streets meet, or the crisp corner of a baking tray.

examples.text: La esquina está aquí.
examples.trans: The corner is here.

examples.text: Vemos las esquinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the corners from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.

examples.text: ¿Dónde están las llaves de latón?
examples.trans: Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.text: Este patio es muy tranquilo.
examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.

examples.text: Esta mañana hace mucho sol.
examples.trans: This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Por favor literally means 'as a favour'.

examples.text: El favor está aquí.
examples.trans: The favour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los favores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the favours from the door.

meanings.note: Costar una fortuna means 'to cost a fortune'; por fortuna means 'fortunately'.

examples.text: Las piedras antiguas del patio cuestan una fortuna.
examples.trans: The old courtyard flagstones cost a fortune.

examples.text: Por fortuna, no entró ni una gota de agua en la caja.
examples.trans: Fortunately, not a single drop of water got into the box.

meanings.note: Plural-only feminine noun in Spain: las gafas.

examples.text: ¿Dónde he dejado mis gafas?
examples.trans: Where did I leave my glasses?

examples.text: Lleva unas gafas redondas.
examples.trans: He wears round glasses.

golpear.gloss: to bump; to knock; to hit

meanings.en: to bump; to knock; to hit
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: No golpees la pared con la caja.
examples.trans: Do not bump the wall with the box.

examples.text: La rama golpeaba suavemente el cristal.
examples.trans: The branch tapped gently against the windowpane.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ya hemos preparado las habitaciones.
examples.trans: We have already prepared the rooms.

hacer.gloss: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)

meanings.en: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)
meanings.note: Irregular: hago, hice, hecho; hace tres años = three years ago.

examples.text: La panadera hace pan fresco cada mañana.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.

examples.text: Llegó hace diez minutos.
examples.trans: She arrived ten minutes ago.

meanings.note: Indicates direction of movement or gaze.

examples.text: Camina hacia el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: Walk toward the stone bridge.

examples.text: Sigue mirando hacia la esquina.
examples.trans: Keep looking toward the corner.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Sonar hueco means 'to sound hollow' when tapped; as a noun (el hueco), it means 'gap, space, or free slot'.

examples.text: Ese tronco viejo está hueco por dentro.
examples.trans: That old tree trunk is hollow inside.

examples.text: Al pisar la tercera piedra del patio, sonó hueca.
examples.trans: When stepping on the third courtyard stone, it sounded hollow.

meanings.note: Used with estar when stating someone is retired (está jubilado) or directly after a profession (un cartógrafo jubilado); also used as a noun.

examples.text: El cartógrafo jubilado envió una postal desde la costa.
examples.trans: The retired mapmaker sent a postcard from the coast.

examples.text: Mi tío está jubilado y pasea cada mañana por el parque.
examples.trans: My uncle is retired and walks through the park every morning.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Preterite 3rd sg/pl spells y: leyó, leyeron; past participle leído.

examples.text: Leo el periódico con el primer café.
examples.trans: I read the newspaper with my first coffee.

examples.text: Anoche leímos toda la carta juntos.
examples.trans: Last night we read the whole letter together.

levantar.gloss: to lift; to raise; to get up (levantarse)

meanings.en: to lift; to raise; to get up (levantarse)
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Levanta esa esquina de la alfombra.
examples.trans: Lift that corner of the rug.

examples.text: Nos levantamos a las seis y media.
examples.trans: We get up at six thirty.

llevar.gloss: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)

meanings.en: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)
meanings.note: Versatile verb for carrying items, wearing clothes/glasses, or duration.

examples.text: Llevo dos tazas calientes al jardín.
examples.trans: I carry two hot cups to the garden.

examples.text: Hoy lleva un abrigo gris oscuro.
examples.trans: Today he is wearing a dark grey coat.

meanings.note: From lluvia, rain: un día lluvioso.

examples.text: Mañana va a ser un día lluvioso.
examples.trans: Tomorrow is going to be a rainy day.

examples.text: El otoño aquí es muy lluvioso.
examples.trans: Autumn here is very rainy.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.text: La madera está aquí.
examples.trans: The wood is here.

examples.text: Vemos las maderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the woods from the door.

mango.gloss: handle (of a tool or pan); mango

meanings.en: handle (of a tool or pan); mango
meanings.note: Watch the gender contrast: masculine el mango is a tool handle (or tropical mango fruit), whereas feminine la manga is a shirt or coat sleeve.

examples.text: Golpee la piedra suavemente con el mango de madera.
examples.trans: Tap the stone gently with the wooden handle.

examples.text: Coge la sartén caliente siempre por el mango.
examples.trans: Always hold the hot frying pan by the handle.

meanings.note: Months are written with a small letter in Spanish: el diez de mayo.

examples.text: Mi cumpleaños es en mayo.
examples.trans: My birthday is in May.

examples.text: Llegamos el tres de mayo.
examples.trans: We arrive on the third of May.

meanings.note: La mañana = the morning; mañana (without article) = tomorrow.

examples.text: Por la mañana servimos café caliente.
examples.trans: In the morning we serve hot coffee.

examples.text: ¡Hasta mañana a las ocho!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow at eight!

meanings.note: Media vuelta = half-turn (turn around); medio vaso = half a glass.

examples.text: Es una pieza media.
examples.trans: It is a half piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: Dining, cafe, or courtyard table.

examples.text: La mesa está aquí.
examples.trans: The table is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mesas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tables from the door.

meter.gloss: to put in; to tuck in

meanings.en: to put in; to tuck in
meanings.note: Everyday Spanish verb specifically for putting something inside a pocket, bag, or drawer.

examples.text: Meto las llaves en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: I put the keys in my pocket.

examples.text: Metimos las sillas dentro por la lluvia.
examples.trans: We brought the chairs inside because of the rain.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.text: Mi maleta es azul marino.
examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Links two simultaneous actions.

examples.text: Espera aquí mientras abro la puerta.
examples.trans: Wait here while I open the door.

examples.text: Preparo el té mientras sale el pan.
examples.trans: I make the tea while the bread comes out.

meanings.note: Accented más means 'more / most'; de más = extra.

examples.text: ¿Quiere un poco más de té?
examples.trans: Would you like a little more tea?

examples.text: Es la habitación más tranquila.
examples.trans: It is the quietest room.

meanings.note: Requires no before the verb when nadie follows (no hay nadie).

examples.text: Todavía no hay nadie en el patio.
examples.trans: There is nobody in the courtyard yet.

examples.text: Nadie conoce mejor este edificio.
examples.trans: Nobody knows this building better.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: Al norte de = 'north of / to the north of'.

examples.text: Las ventanas frescas miran hacia el norte del jardín.
examples.trans: The cool windows face toward the north of the garden.

examples.text: Su familia vive en un pueblo verde del norte de España.
examples.trans: His family lives in a green village in northern Spain.

meanings.note: Written after street names in Spanish addresses (Calle Mayor número ocho).

examples.text: El número está aquí.
examples.trans: The number is here.

examples.text: Vemos los números desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the numbers from the door.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Oír pasos = to hear footsteps.

examples.text: El paso está aquí.
examples.trans: The footstep is here.

examples.text: Vemos los pasos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the footsteps from the door.

pata.gloss: leg (of furniture or an animal); paw

meanings.en: leg (of furniture or an animal); paw
meanings.note: Used for animal legs/paws and the legs of tables, chairs, and beds; human legs are las piernas.

examples.text: Levanta la mesa despacio para que no raspen las patas.
examples.trans: Lift the table slowly so the legs do not scrape.

examples.text: Mateo niveló las cuatro patas de la silla de madera.
examples.trans: Mateo levelled all four legs of the wooden chair.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.text: El patio está aquí.
examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Hermano pequeño = younger brother; de pequeño = as a child.

examples.text: Es una pieza pequeña.
examples.trans: It is a small piece.

examples.text: Hay una pequeña tarjeta de cartón atada al asa.
examples.trans: There is a small cardboard card tied to the handle.

meanings.note: De piedra = made of stone.

examples.text: La piedra está aquí.
examples.trans: The stone is here.

examples.text: Vemos las piedras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stones from the door.

meanings.note: In a mystery or treasure hunt, una pista is a clue; also means a dance floor (pista de baile) or sports court (pista de tenis).

examples.text: Lee la pista de la postal una vez más, Clara.
examples.trans: Read the clue on the postcard one more time, Clara.

examples.text: Seguimos las cuatro pistas por la calle de los Tilos.
examples.trans: We followed all four clues along Calle de los Tilos.

meanings.note: Architectural drawing or city street map.

examples.text: El plano está aquí.
examples.trans: The blueprint is here.

examples.text: Vemos los planos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the blueprints from the door.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Short for tarjeta postal.

examples.text: La postal está aquí.
examples.trans: The postcard is here.

examples.text: Vemos las postales desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the postcards from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.text: ¡Hasta pronto y buen viaje!
examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.

meanings.note: Mi propia maleta = my own suitcase.

examples.text: Es una pieza propia.
examples.trans: It is an own piece.

examples.text: ¿Y no pidió su propia maleta con el tren de madera?
examples.trans: And he did not ask for his own suitcase with the wooden train?

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.text: La puerta está aquí.
examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

raspar.gloss: to scrape; to scratch; to grate

meanings.en: to scrape; to scratch; to grate
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb for metal or wood scraping against stone, or for grating zest in the kitchen.

examples.text: Levanta la mesa para que las patas no raspen el suelo.
examples.trans: Lift the table so the legs do not scrape the floor.

examples.text: Rocío raspó un poco de piel de limón sobre la masa.
examples.trans: Rocío grated a little lemon peel over the batter.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Las seis = six o'clock.

examples.text: Me despierto a las seis y media.
examples.trans: I wake up at six thirty.

examples.text: Tengo seis limones en la cesta.
examples.trans: I have six lemons in the basket.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.text: Solo necesito cinco minutos más.
examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.

examples.text: Queda una sola habitación libre.
examples.trans: Only a single room remains vacant.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suena).

examples.text: El despertador suena a las seis y media.
examples.trans: The alarm clock rings at six thirty.

examples.text: El piano sonaba cálido bajo la lluvia.
examples.trans: The piano sounded warm in the rain.

examples.text: El enchufe está un poco suelto.
examples.trans: The socket is a bit loose.

examples.text: Lleva una camisa suelta.
examples.trans: She's wearing a loose shirt.

meanings.note: Onomatopoeic regular -ar verb whose repeated s and r sounds echo a soft whisper.

examples.text: ¡Susurrad los dos, que los huéspedes todavía duermen!
examples.trans: Whisper, both of you—the guests are still sleeping!

examples.text: Carmen le susurró un secreto al oído a Rocío.
examples.trans: Carmen whispered a secret in Rocío's ear.

meanings.note: El sábado means 'on Saturday'; los sábados means 'on Saturdays'.

examples.text: Los sábados vamos temprano al mercado de la plaza.
examples.trans: On Saturdays we go early to the market in the square.

examples.text: Este sábado abrimos las ventanas de la galería.
examples.trans: This Saturday we open the sunroom windows.

meanings.note: Shortened form of tanto used before adjectives and adverbs (¡qué mañana tan luminosa!).

examples.text: ¡Qué patio tan tranquilo!
examples.trans: What a peaceful courtyard!

examples.text: ¿Por qué sale el agua tan fría?
examples.trans: Why is the water running so cold?

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.text: Tenemos ocho habitaciones tranquilas.
examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

tocar.gloss: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)

meanings.en: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)
meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: toqué.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de tocar el timbre.
examples.trans: Someone just rang the bell.

examples.text: De niño tocaba el piano los viernes.
examples.trans: As a boy he played the piano on Fridays.

meanings.note: Treinta y cinco = thirty-five.

examples.text: Nos dan treinta días de plazo.
examples.trans: They give us thirty days' notice.

examples.text: Son las nueve y treinta y cinco.
examples.trans: It is nine thirty-five.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.

examples.text: Empieza con tres frases cortas.
examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Shortens to un before masculine singular nouns.

examples.text: Toma uno recién salido del horno.
examples.trans: Take one fresh out of the oven.

examples.text: Contamos del uno al ocho.
examples.trans: We count from one to eight.

meanings.note: El verano que viene = next summer.

examples.text: El verano está aquí.
examples.trans: The summer is here.

examples.text: Vemos los veranos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the summers from the door.

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.text: La verdad está aquí.
examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

vez.gloss: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)

meanings.en: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)
meanings.note: Plural las veces; a veces = sometimes; otra vez = again.

examples.text: La vez está aquí.
examples.trans: The time / occasion is here.

examples.text: Vemos las veces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the time / occasions from the door.

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.text: Es una pieza vieja.
examples.trans: It is an old piece.

examples.text: La vieja buhardilla soleada... ¡seguidme, rápido!
examples.trans: The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Plural los árboles.

examples.text: El árbol está aquí.
examples.trans: The tree is here.

examples.text: Vemos los árboles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trees from the door.
